answer: Let each bond slowly evaporate: a demurrage bleeds the stake every epoch unless refilled from fresh outside funds. One honest agent tops up a single bond, a steady jade drip it barely notices. A farm cannot amortize: a thousand decaying bonds each demand their own continuous refill from a real external source, so the carrying cost rises like a nebula of outflows expanding every epoch, never settling. The stake cannot be recycled head-to-head because each is draining at once; maintaining N live identities burns N streams of fresh capital, an ever-climbing ridge no single honest agent faces.
